overlaps.paper_title: Analysis of a complete DNA–protein affinity landscape
overlaps.definition_quote: Jones and Forrest, §3, p. 2: ‘r = c_FD/(σ_F σ_D)’; Hamming distance is to the closest global maximum. GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/correlation.py:105–147: fdc(..., method='spearman') accepts both ‘spearman’ and ‘pearson’ and correlates fitness with distance to the global optimum.
overlaps.definition_divergence: GraphFLA defaults to Spearman rank correlation. A Pearson call is required to match the original product-moment FDC definition used by Rowe et al.; no calculation was made because the Rowe input was unavailable.

input.preprocessing: The paper-listed data URL returned HTTP 404; see blockers and acquisition_codex.jsonl.

overlaps.reason: The article says the experimental data are available at http://dbkgroup.org/direvol.htm, but that URL and its HTTPS form returned HTTP 404. No source-data file was recovered; the printed value was not read from a plot.

overlaps.paper_title: Analysis of a complete DNA–protein affinity landscape
overlaps.locator: §3.5, ‘Autocorrelation function and correlation length’; Figure 2 is referenced in the prose
overlaps.definition_quote: Rowe et al., §3.5: ‘expected correlation ... during a random walk’. GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/ruggedness.py:46–85: ‘The lag-``lag`` autocorrelation of fitness, pooled across all random walks under a single grand mean.’
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper prints the exponential decay length τ, whereas GraphFLA returns the autocorrelation coefficient at one selected lag (default lag 1). The published prose estimate is recorded as printed; no value was read off Figure 2. Raw input was also unavailable, so no transform or refit was attempted.

input.preprocessing: Same inaccessible Rowe 10-mer input as the FDC and peak-count targets.

overlaps.reason: The value is a fitted correlation length, not a lag-specific autocorrelation. The paper-listed raw data URL also returned HTTP 404.

overlaps.paper_value_unit: mean number of neutral mutant neighbors per genotype in the modeled RNA neutral network
overlaps.locator: Results, ‘RNA Evolution on Structurally Neutral Networks’
overlaps.definition_quote: van Nimwegen et al., Abstract: ‘average number of neutral mutant neighbors ... matrix spectral radius.’ GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/robustness.py:157–179: ‘the proportion of neighbors with fitness values within a given threshold’.
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper reports network degree and population-weighted neutrality on an RNA folding neutral network; GraphFLA returns a normalized fraction of neighbors within a fitness-difference threshold. The paper’s map is simulated RNA secondary structure, not a measured empirical fitness landscape. No GraphFLA run was made.

input.preprocessing: Model-defined RNA network; no genotype-fitness input table was deposited with the article.

overlaps.reason: A useful theoretical neutrality result, but its counted degree/population statistic and modeled RNA map are not a GraphFLA empirical neutrality target. No numerical neutrality value on an obtainable measured landscape above the requested size threshold was found.

overlaps.locator: Family-level screen of empirical landscape papers
overlaps.definition_quote: GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/robustness.py:157–179 defines a neighbor-fraction threshold statistic. The reviewed empirical papers did not state a matching large-landscape neutrality fraction.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Conceptual RNA neutral-network papers report network degree or population robustness, while the empirical landscape papers reviewed here did not print a directly comparable GraphFLA neutrality value.
overlaps.reason: No eligible printed neutrality fraction on an obtainable real landscape was found.

overlaps.paper_title: Adaptation in protein fitness landscapes is facilitated by indirect paths
overlaps.definition_quote: Wu et al., Results: ‘all 15 fitness peaks’. GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/navigability.py:120–135: ‘the fraction of configurations in the landscape that can reach the global optimum via any monotonic, fitness-improving path.’
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper’s denominator is genotypes able to access every one of 15 wild-type-beneficial peaks under its adaptive-path analysis. GraphFLA global_optima_accessibility asks whether configurations can reach the single global optimum. The publisher data are available, but the paper’s reported target is not the same statistic.

input.preprocessing: Measured and author-imputed tables combined as deposited; no new accessibility run because of target definition mismatch.

overlaps.reason: The published accessibility is an all-15-peaks intersection, not accessibility to the single global optimum.

overlaps.paper_title: A rugged yet easily navigable fitness landscape
overlaps.paper_value_unit: percent of simulated adaptive walks reaching a high-fitness peak
overlaps.locator: Results, ‘Adaptive evolution can easily reach high fitness peaks via short paths’, p. 3
overlaps.definition_quote: Papkou et al., Results p. 3; GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/navigability.py:120–135: fraction of all configurations able to reach the one global optimum by any monotonic improving path.
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper reports the endpoint fraction across simulated adaptive walks and a set of high-fitness peaks. GraphFLA reports a configuration-level reachability fraction for the single highest-fitness genotype.

input.preprocessing: Existing curated functional component; no run because the paper’s value is an adaptive-walk endpoint fraction.

overlaps.reason: The paper’s walk-level simulation statistic is not the GraphFLA graph-reachability fraction.

overlaps.paper_title: A thousand empirical adaptive landscapes and their navigability
overlaps.quote: accessible paths to the highest-affinity site
overlaps.definition_quote: GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/navigability.py:120–135: fraction of configurations with any monotonic path to the global optimum.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Peak accessibility is a fraction of shortest paths to the highest-affinity site; GraphFLA counts configurations that can reach the global optimum. The article’s individual values are plotted, and no point was read from the plot.

input.preprocessing: PBM data are identified as public in UniPROBE/CIS-BP; no individual printed numerical target was available.

overlaps.reason: The paper supplies a plotted path-fraction distribution, not a printed single-landscape GraphFLA configuration fraction.

overlaps.paper_title: A rugged yet easily navigable fitness landscape
overlaps.definition_quote: Papkou et al., Figure 3D caption; GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/navigability.py:300–329: ‘mean shortest path length to the global optimum.’
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper aggregates accessible shortest paths from variants to high-fitness peaks, not distances to only the single global optimum. The fitted target differs even though both use shortest accessible paths.

input.preprocessing: Existing curated functional component; no run because the paper’s target is across high-fitness peaks.

overlaps.reason: The target pools variant-to-high-peak paths rather than measuring paths to the one global optimum.

overlaps.paper_title: Analysis of a complete DNA–protein affinity landscape
overlaps.paper_value_unit: mean Hamming distance from each sequence to local optima
overlaps.locator: Table 3, row ‘distance from every sequence to local optima’
overlaps.definition_quote: Rowe et al., Table 3: ‘distance from every sequence to local optima’. GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/navigability.py:422–441: ‘mean distance from all configurations to the global optimum.’
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper reports distance to the nearest local optimum, not distance to the global optimum. The source data are also unavailable at the paper-listed URL.

overlaps.paper_title: A rugged yet easily navigable fitness landscape
overlaps.locator: Results, p. 2; Figure S12 cited in text
overlaps.definition_quote: Papkou et al., p. 2: ‘variants from which a peak is accessible.’ GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/correlation.py:205–238: correlates local-optimum fitness with `size_basin_greedy`, the deterministic greedy basin size.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Papkou’s basin counts every variant with an accessible increasing path to a peak, so variants can belong to multiple peak basins. GraphFLA assigns a greedy basin. No run was made because the basin definitions differ.

input.preprocessing: Existing curated functional component; available, but basin statistic is incompatible.

overlaps.reason: The published basin is an accessible-ancestor set, not GraphFLA’s greedy assignment basin.

overlaps.paper_title: Analysis of a complete DNA–protein affinity landscape
overlaps.definition_quote: Rowe et al., §3.7: basins are the points in the landscape ‘that are attracted to each optimum’ under its steepest-ascent hill-climber. GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/correlation.py:205–238: correlation of local-optimum fitness with greedy basin size.
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper reports only a qualitative sign, not a numeric correlation coefficient or its correlation method. Its basin assignment is steepest ascent, which is conceptually close to GraphFLA’s greedy basin, but no numerical target exists.
overlaps.reason: Qualitative negative relationship only; the paper prints no numeric coefficient to reproduce.

overlaps.paper_title: Adaptation in protein fitness landscapes is facilitated by indirect paths
overlaps.locator: Results, ‘Two distinct mechanisms of extra-dimensional bypass’; Figure 2 caption
overlaps.definition_quote: Conrad, p. 68: ‘extradimensional bypass’. GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/epistasis/motifs.py:387–423: proportion of reciprocal-sign-epistasis type-19 motifs for which a bypass exists.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Wu et al. report separate conversion and detour success frequencies for sampled reciprocal-sign interactions, with different pathway operations and denominators. GraphFLA counts motifs with any accessible bypass across the full type-19 motif set. The publisher’s 160,000-variant data are available, but these percentages are not the same statistic.

input.preprocessing: Measured and author-imputed tables combined as deposited; no motif run because the denominators/operations differ.

overlaps.reason: The printed conversion and detour proportions do not use GraphFLA’s motif-level bypass denominator.

overlaps.paper_title: Adaptation in protein fitness landscapes is facilitated by indirect paths
overlaps.locator: Results, ‘Indirect paths promote evolutionary accessibility’; Methods, ‘Predicting fitness landscape and identifying epistasis types’
overlaps.definition_quote: Wu et al., Methods: ‘0 out-degree’; Results: ‘160,000 variants’. GraphFLA graphfla/landscape/_optima.py:7–33: ‘n_lo’ is ‘Number of distinct local optima’; each plateau local optimum counts once.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Both count genotypes with no strictly improving Hamming-1 neighbor. GraphFLA’s plateau-aware rule is additional; on this input the independent zero-outdegree count and GraphFLA n_lo both equal the paper’s count, with no plateau local optima.

input.preprocessing: Combined 149,361 measured and 10,639 imputed rows as deposited; no extra normalization; epsilon=0.

overlaps.reason: GraphFLA n_lo=30 and the paper’s stated zero-outdegree peak rule both count 30. The input’s canonical sequence/fitness SHA-256 is recorded above. Read-only XLSX parsing emitted an openpyxl unsupported-extension warning; source workbooks were not saved.

overlaps.paper_title: A rugged yet easily navigable fitness landscape
overlaps.locator: Results, ‘The fitness landscape is rugged’, p. 2
overlaps.definition_quote: Papkou et al., p. 2: ‘higher fitness than all their one-mutant neighbors’; ‘135,178’. GraphFLA graphfla/landscape/_optima.py:7–33: n_lo counts distinct local optima, with each plateau optimum counted once.

overlaps.paper_title: Analysis of a complete DNA–protein affinity landscape
overlaps.definition_quote: Rowe et al., §3.7: ‘no neighbour fitter’. GraphFLA graphfla/landscape/_optima.py:7–33 counts distinct strict optima and collapses local-optimum plateaus.
overlaps.definition_divergence: The local-maximum rule is compatible if ties are absent; the article does not state whether exact ties were collapsed as plateaus, and the data were not recovered to check. The paper’s 10-mer measurements exceed the requested landscape-size threshold, but its cited download URL now returns HTTP 404.

overlaps.paper_title: A thousand empirical adaptive landscapes and their navigability
overlaps.paper_value: 2–36 peaks across the 1,137 landscapes; 478 of 1,137 (42%) have multiple peaks
overlaps.locator: Results, ‘Adaptive landscapes of TF binding affinity’ and ‘Landscape navigability: the number of peaks’; Figure 2a caption
overlaps.definition_quote: Aguilar-Rodríguez et al., Methods: ‘all ... neighbours ... lower’. GraphFLA graphfla/landscape/_optima.py:7–33 counts distinct local optima and collapses local-optimum plateaus.
overlaps.definition_divergence: The underlying statistic is compatible after matching the paper’s PBM thresholds and plateau rule. The printed result is a corpus-level range and multiple-peak fraction, not a named single-landscape n_lo. The paper points to public UniPROBE/CIS-BP data, but the publisher’s Supplementary Table 1 retrieval returned an HTML security challenge, and no TF-to-landscape matrix set was acquired for a corpus-wide run.

input.preprocessing: Paper says the PBM inputs are public in UniPROBE/CIS-BP; Supplementary Table 1 mapping was not retrieved.

overlaps.graphfla_call: Repeated n_lo calls on each article-defined TF landscape, followed by counting landscapes with n_lo>1 (not run)
overlaps.reason: A printed aggregate target exists, but the inputs and mapping needed to rebuild the 1,137 landscape corpus were not obtained; no plotted peak-count point was read.

overlaps.locator: Core-literature search across the verified references
overlaps.definition_quote: GraphFLA graphfla/analysis/ruggedness.py:20–43: local_optima_ratio is n_lo divided by n_configs. The reviewed papers report peak counts or other summaries; no direct printed local-optima-per-configuration ratio was found.
overlaps.definition_divergence: A ratio could be derived from some published peak counts, but that derived value is not a published target and was not manufactured as a reproduction target.
overlaps.reason: The direct statistic local_optima_ratio is not reported in the reviewed papers.
